title: Replace orders.shipped with a fulfillment_status enum
summary: Four operations in two phases, each one online, to retire the legacy boolean without a long lock on a 3M-row table.

blocks.title: Motivation
blocks.text:
`orders.shipped` and `orders.status` can disagree: the warehouse job sets the flag while a cancelled order keeps `status = 'cancelled'`. Reporting special-cases both. One typed column, `fulfillment_status`, replaces the flag and the free-text status check.

The table has ~3.1M rows and takes writes continuously, so every step must avoid an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock held for longer than a few milliseconds.

operations.title: Create the enum type
operations.detail: A Postgres enum. Adding a value later is `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`, which is online but cannot run inside a transaction block before Postgres 12. Removing a value is not supported; that is the cost of an enum over a lookup table.

operations.title: Add the column, nullable, no default
operations.code:
ALTER TABLE orders
  ADD COLUMN fulfillment_status fulfillment_status;
operations.before:
status        text    not null default 'pending'
shipped       boolean not null default false
operations.after:
status             text               not null default 'pending'
shipped            boolean            not null default false
fulfillment_status fulfillment_status null
operations.detail:
Adding a nullable column with no default is a catalog-only change: the lock is `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` but held for microseconds, no rewrite.

A `NOT NULL` or a non-constant default here would rewrite the table. The constraint comes later, after the backfill.
operations.locks: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for the catalog update only; waits behind long-running transactions, so run with `lock_timeout = '2s'` and retry.
operations.rollback: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN fulfillment_status;

operations.title: Backfill in batches of 10k by id
operations.code:
UPDATE orders
SET fulfillment_status = CASE
  WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 'cancelled'
  WHEN shipped AND status = 'delivered' THEN 'delivered'
  WHEN shipped THEN 'shipped'
  ELSE status::fulfillment_status
END
WHERE id BETWEEN $1 AND $1 + 9999
  AND fulfillment_status IS NULL;
operations.detail:
Run from a script that walks `id` in 10k steps with a short sleep between batches. Each batch touches one index range, holds row locks only, and commits.

The `CASE` encodes the precedence: `cancelled` wins over the flag, and the flag promotes `shipped` only when status has not already moved past it. The application starts writing `fulfillment_status` on every insert and update **before** this runs, so the backfill only has to cover old rows; the `IS NULL` guard makes it safe to re-run.
operations.locks: Row locks per batch. Bloat from ~3.1M updated rows; autovacuum handles it, or run a manual VACUUM after.
operations.rollback: Nothing to undo: dropping the column (op 2 rollback) discards the data.
warnings: Orders inserted between the column add and the application deploy will have NULL until the backfill reaches them. Verify with `SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE fulfillment_status IS NULL` before phase 2.

operations.title: Enforce NOT NULL without a full scan lock
operations.detail: The direct `SET NOT NULL` scans the table under `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE`. The four-statement form adds the check `NOT VALID` (instant), validates it under a `SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE` lock that allows writes, and then `SET NOT NULL` recognises the validated check and skips its own scan (Postgres 12+).
operations.locks: SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE during VALIDATE; brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for the other three statements.
operations.rollback: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN fulfillment_status DROP NOT NULL;

operations.title: Drop the legacy flag
operations.code: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN shipped;
operations.before:
shipped            boolean            not null default false
fulfillment_status fulfillment_status not null
operations.detail: Catalog-only; the data stays on disk until rows are rewritten. Do this one release after the application stops reading `shipped`, so a rollback of the app does not meet a missing column.
operations.rollback: Re-add the column and recompute it from fulfillment_status: `shipped = fulfillment_status IN ('shipped','delivered')`. The original values are lost, but they are derivable.
warnings: Not reversible without a backfill. Search the codebase and dashboards for `shipped` before merging.

phases.title: Phase 1 · additive, this release
phases.detail: Deploy the app change that writes both columns, then run ops 1 to 4.

phases.title: Phase 2 · destructive, next release
phases.detail: After one release with no reader of `shipped`.

questions.prompt: Enum type or lookup table for the status set?

options.label: Postgres enum
options.detail: Compact, typed, no join. Values cannot be removed.

options.label: Lookup table with FK
options.detail: Values editable at runtime; one more join on hot paths.

questions.prompt: Backfill batch size and pacing. Pick what the write load tolerates.
Anything else that reads `orders.shipped` that the agent should know about before phase 2?
